title: History 15: The size era: FP8, GGUF and 4-bit formats arrive

questions.q: Why is int4 with one scale ruined by 0.1% outliers, while int4 with a scale per 16 isn't?
options: An outlier widens the grid for everyone sharing its scale, so block scales confine the damage
Block scales use more bits per code
Outliers are removed by the block format
int4 can't store outliers at all
questions.answer: An outlier widens the grid for everyone sharing its scale, so block scales confine the damage
questions.why: In the lab 0.192 goes to 0.733 with one scale, and 0.085 to 0.090 with a scale per 16.

questions.q: Why does fp8 hardly notice the same outliers?
options: It is a float, so a large value costs precision only near that value
It stores outliers separately
It clips them to zero
It uses 16 bits for them
questions.answer: It is a float, so a large value costs precision only near that value
questions.why: Spacing grows with the value, so small weights keep their own fine spacing.

questions.q: Your card has no fast kernel for a format. What do the layers do?
options: They keep the small weights and expand them for the multiply, so you keep the memory saving and lose the speed
They load as fp32 for good, losing the memory saving
They refuse to load
They run on the CPU only
questions.answer: They keep the small weights and expand them for the multiply, so you keep the memory saving and lose the speed
questions.why: get_disabled_quant_formats marks the format, and the test shows a plain tensor reaching linear.

questions.q: A 14 B parameter model at 4.5 bits per weight is 7.3 GiB of weights. Will it run on an 8 GB card?
options: That number doesn't settle it: text encoder, VAE and working memory are extra
Yes, 7.3 is below 8
No, 4.5 bit files never run
Yes, because the VAE is in the same file
questions.answer: That number doesn't settle it: text encoder, VAE and working memory are extra
questions.why: The table is weights alone. CU-305 works out the budget.

questions.q: Is GGUF a way of rounding weights?
options: No. It is a file format that holds tensors of several types, such as Q8_0 and Q4_K
Yes, it is a 4-bit rounding method
Yes, it replaces fp8
No, it is a ComfyUI core loader
questions.answer: No. It is a file format that holds tensors of several types, such as Q8_0 and Q4_K
questions.why: The specification defines a file layout and lists ggml types. Core ComfyUI doesn't load it.
